# Nexus Code: Local AI Coding Harness & TUI

> An autonomous & interactive software engineering harness comparable to **OpenAI Codex CLI** and **Anthropic Claude Code**, engineered specifically for **local LLMs** (vLLM, LM Studio) on **Linux** using **Rust + TypeScript**.

---

## ⚡ Core Highlights

| Feature | Nexus Code | Codex / Claude Code Equivalent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Interactive REPL & TUI** | Default interactive prompt with model/git status badges | `claude` / `codex` interactive terminal |
| **Autonomous Multi-Step Agent** | Multi-turn ReAct loop with self-correcting error recovery | `claude -p "..."` / `codex exec` |
| **Human Review / Approval Mode** | Colorized unified diff preview before modifying files | Claude Code interactive permission prompts |
| **Project Memory & Rules** | Automatically loads `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `CODEX.md` | Claude Code Memory (`CLAUDE.md`) |
| **Git Repository Intelligence** | Live branch and uncommitted change indicators in prompt | Git status context awareness |
| **Persistent Prompt History** | Arrow-key navigation saved across sessions to `~/.nexus_history` | Readline / shell history |
| **Context Compaction** | `/compact` command to prune history and retain token headroom | Claude Code `/compact` |
| **Engine Speed** | Rust-powered Ripgrep search, safe diff patcher, and file finder | Native Ripgrep / AST engine |

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Interactive Session (REPL / TUI)
Simply run `harness` (or `nexus`) from any directory or git repository:
```bash
harness
```
*Prompt:*
```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║           NEXUS CODE HARNESS - CODEX / CLAUDE-CODE REPL        ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
Type your prompt or task, or type /help for slash commands.

Session Status:
  • Workspace:   /home/mike/Projects/my-app (my-app) [git: main *2]
  • Model:       engineering/b0
  • Endpoint:    http://127.0.0.1:18010/v1
  • Shell:       bash
  • Mode:        auto (autonomous execution)
  • Context:     1 messages in memory

nexus (engineering/b0) my-app:main*2 ❯ 
```

### 2. Autonomous Single-Shot Mode
To run a specific task and exit:
```bash
harness run "Inspect the project, write comprehensive unit tests, and verify with cargo test"
```

For worktree-isolated runs, automatic merge requires an explicitly trusted verifier command. Configure it with `--authoritative-verifier "make test"` (or the corresponding `authoritativeVerifierCommand` in `HarnessConfig`). Automatically discovered test commands can still provide diagnostic evidence, but success alone does not authorize merging a worktree.

### Turn outcomes and exit codes

Every turn returns one structured result with three independent dimensions (`cli/src/core/turn.ts`):

| Dimension | Values |
| :--- | :--- |
| `execution` | `COMPLETED`, `INTERRUPTED`, `FAILED`, `BLOCKED`, `LIMIT_REACHED` |
| `outcome` | `VERIFIED` (selected verifier ran and passed), `UNVERIFIED` (changes made, not verified; see `reason`, e.g. `NO_APPLICABLE_VERIFIER`, `VERIFICATION_NOT_RUN`), `NOT_ESTABLISHED`, `NOT_REQUIRED` (no workspace change) |
| `acceptance` | `NOT_REQUESTED` (Nexus never sets `ACCEPTED`) |

A model that stops calling tools has only stopped; it has not demonstrated anything. `harness run` exits **0** for verified or nothing-to-verify completion, **2** for completed-but-unverified, **130** when interrupted, and **1** for failure, blocked, step-limit or unverified-verifier-failure. `--json` output carries the full `turn` object and `exitCode`.

Ctrl-C while a turn is running requests cancellation: no new inference request or tool dispatch is admitted, and a tool that is already executing is awaited (it cannot be force-stopped). A second Ctrl-C terminates immediately. At an idle prompt Ctrl-C exits the REPL.

### Legacy readline REPL (`harness --repl`)

The default interface is the live TUI, which has a real multi-line composer. The legacy REPL reads one line at a time: lines that arrive together with a prompt (a multi-line paste, piped input) or while a turn is running cannot become prompts. They are not silently dropped: the REPL prints how many lines were ignored and the first one. To submit multi-line input there, wrap it in `"""` … `"""` (or ```` ``` ````), or use the TUI.

# Nexus Code Architecture

Nexus Code utilizes a split architecture designed for performance, modularity, and security:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 TypeScript Orchestration Layer              │
│   • REPL / TUI Interface        • Agent Intelligence        │
│   • Skills Engine               • MCP JSON-RPC Client       │
│   • Plugin Lifecycle System     • Checkpoint & Undo Engine  │
│   • Secret Redactor             • Session Persistence       │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │ IPC / CLI Subprocess
┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│                    Rust Core Engine (ELF)                   │
│   • Path Resolution Jail        • Ripgrep Fast Search       │
│   • Atomic File Ops             • AST Symbol Parser         │
│   • Patch / Diff Applicator     • Tree & Metadata Inspector │
│   • POSIX Command Runner        • Destructive Command Guard │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │ HTTP / SSE Gateway
┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│                  Local Inference Hardware                   │
│   • vLLM / LM Studio Gateway (port 18010/v1)                │
│   • Dual Intel Arc A770 XPUs (engineering/b0 model)         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Rust Core Engine (`core/`)

The core engine is implemented in Rust 2024 edition and compiled into an optimized 64-bit ELF binary (`harness-core`).
- **`file_ops.rs`**: Safe reading, writing, atomic replacement, metadata inspection (`file_info`), batch reading (`batch_read`), unified patch application (`patch_file`), and path traversal prevention (`resolve_safe_path`).
- **`search.rs`**: Fast ripgrep search using `ignore` and `grep` crates, regex symbol extraction across multi-language ASTs, and Unicode file tree formatting (`file_tree`).
- **`runner.rs`**: Child process execution with strict timeouts, buffer truncations, and destructive pattern detection (`is_dangerous_command`).

---

## 2. TypeScript Orchestration Layer (`cli/`)

- **`AutonomousAgent` (`agent.ts`)**: Manages the iterative decision loop, token budgeting, prompt construction, and tool execution.
- **`InteractiveRepl` (`repl.ts`)**: TUI terminal interface with tab autocompletion, multiline input, direct shell escapes, and slash commands.
- **`LocalLlmClient` (`client.ts`)**: Streaming SSE OpenAI-compatible client with automatic auth token discovery and token rotation retry.
- **`CheckpointManager` (`checkpoint.ts`)**: Creates safe git and tree checkpoints before every turn and manages workspace rollbacks (`/undo`).
- **`McpClientManager` (`mcp.ts`)**: Stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 client connecting external MCP servers from `~/.config/nexus/mcp.json`.
- **`SkillManager` (`skills.ts`)**: Auto-discovers and dynamically loads `SKILL.md` documents on-demand.
- **`PluginManager` (`plugins.ts`)**: Lifecycle hook manager supporting `onTurnStart`, `onToolCall`, `onToolResult`, and custom tool registration.
- **`TerminalUI` (`ui.ts`)**: Formatted terminal output with live spinners, colored diffs, milestone plans, and secret scrubber.

---

## 3. Extensibility & Security Boundaries

1. **Workspace Path Jail**: All file operations canonicalize paths against the root workspace directory. Traversal outside the root or requests targeting sensitive system directories (`/etc/shadow`, `~/.ssh`) are rejected with `Security Violation`.
2. **Dangerous Command Filter**: Shell commands are analyzed for destructive signatures (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, raw device writes, fork bombs) and prevented before child execution.
3. **Secret Redaction**: Terminal outputs and audit logs are filtered through regular expression scrubbers that mask Bearer tokens, private keys, passwords, and API credentials.
4. **Audit Trail**: Every tool invocation is permanently recorded in `~/.nexus/audit.log`.

- Maintain documentation integrity and keep existing comments.
- Always run tests after making changes to verify correctness.
- Keep functions modular and clearly typed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nexus Code Security Lifecycle Gates (WP-11, INC-12, SCAN-001..SCAN-005, REL-001..REL-004)
# Enforces non-bypassable pre-commit, build, and release security gates.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

echo "========================================================"
echo "  NEXUS CODE LIFECYCLE SECURITY SCANNING GATES (INC-12) "
echo "========================================================"

# SCAN-002 / SCAN-004: Non-bypassable check. Any attempt to bypass fails the gate.
if [[ -n "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES:-}" && "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES}" != "0" && "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES}" != "false" ]]; then
  echo "[-] ERROR [SCAN-002]: Security gates are non-bypassable. SKIP_SECURITY_GATES is prohibited." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -n "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN:-}" && "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN}" != "0" && "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN}" != "false" ]]; then
  echo "[-] ERROR [SCAN-002]: Security gates are non-bypassable. BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN is prohibited." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gate 1: Dependency Vulnerability Audit (SCAN-001, SCAN-004)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[*] [Gate 1] Auditing Node.js dependencies via npm audit..."
cd "${ROOT_DIR}/cli"
if ! npm audit --audit-level=high; then
  echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-004]: High or Critical vulnerability detected in Node.js dependencies." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "[+] [Gate 1] Node.js dependencies clean (zero High/Critical vulnerabilities)."

echo "[*] [Gate 1] Verifying Rust core dependencies..."
cd "${ROOT_DIR}/core"
if [[ ! -f "Cargo.lock" ]]; then
  echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-001]: Missing Cargo.lock in core crate." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -n "${SIMULATE_RUST_SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE:-}" && "${SIMULATE_RUST_SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
  echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-001]: Rust vulnerability scanner unavailable. Security gates cannot establish dependency safety." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if command -v cargo-audit &>/dev/null; then
  if ! cargo audit; then
    echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-002]: cargo audit reported vulnerability in Rust core dependencies." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
elif [[ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/audit_rust_deps.py" ]]; then
  if ! python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/audit_rust_deps.py" "${ROOT_DIR}/core/Cargo.lock"; then
    echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-002]: Vulnerability audit detected issue in Rust core dependencies." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "[-] FAIL [SCAN-001]: Rust vulnerability scanner unavailable. Security gates cannot establish dependency safety." >&2

content.text:
I read the architecture docs and code layout, ran both test suites, and drew on the dogfooding and compaction findings already in your work-state notes. I did not do a line-by-line audit. Treat the claims below as well-supported, not exhaustive.

Test results: Rust passes (142 TUI tests, 15 core tests). The CLI has 2 failures, `SCAN-001`/`SCAN-004`, which are the known baseline failures. They fail because `npm audit` errors out on `--allow-scripts` in this environment, not because of any code defect.

## What it gets right

1. **Completion semantics.** `cli/src/core/turn.ts` splits a turn into three independent fields: `execution`, `outcome` and `acceptance`. "The model stopped calling tools" is not treated as "the work is done". `UNVERIFIED` is a real state with its own exit code (2), and Nexus never sets `ACCEPTED`. Most agent harnesses get this wrong.
2. **Failure is a first-class result.** The D2–D4 fixes reflect this: context-capacity refusal is a bounded `BLOCKED` result, timeouts are an outcome, and process groups are killed so nothing is orphaned. Each fix has a RED/GREEN test.
3. **Honest limits.** The README documents the legacy REPL's multiline limitation and explains why Ctrl-C can't force-stop a running tool. Bounded defects are labeled `BOUNDED`.
4. **Authority and evidence model.** `authority.ts`, `egress.ts`, `persistence_protection.ts` and the receipt ledger put policy in a separate layer from the agent loop. Worktree auto-merge requires an explicitly trusted verifier.
5. **TUI engineering.** The Rust TUI has 142 tests. Terminal-specific bugs, like the `^H` backspace, get reproduced with a PTY and then fixed.
6. **Process.** Pre-registered experiments, a commit history of fix/feat/test/docs only, and independent review documents per work package.

## Where it needs improvement

1. **The agent core is the bottleneck, not the inference stack.** Your own C2/E3 experiments found that the agent reaches decisive evidence and fails to act on it. Tool-delivered observations get ignored, and how the evidence is delivered determines whether it's used. `agent.ts` is 2,537 lines and `harness.test.ts` is 3,556, so both are hard to change safely.
2. **Verification doesn't handle a dirty baseline.** In the dogfood T2 run, the agent edited at step 9, then looped for 21 steps. `task_completed` kept being rejected because `make test` fails on the known SCAN baseline. That is your Part C item, baseline-aware verification, and it's still open.
3. **Compaction and context management.** Compaction continues to lose engineering continuity. Candidate C2 exists but isn't merged. `tokens.ts` also estimates tokens as `chars / 4`, which is poor for code and doesn't match the local model's actual tokenizer.
4. **Repo hygiene.**
   - `cli/dist/` is tracked (57 files) even though `make clean` deletes it and `verify-reproducibility` rebuilds it.
   - `experiments/` is 322 MB.
   - There are 38 uncommitted files, almost all Cloudflare-contest docs.
   - About 25 `ISSUE12`/`PHASE*`/`WP*` assessment documents sit beside `ARCHITECTURE.md`, which makes the real design hard to find.
   - The package is still named `local-code-harness`, and `harness`/`nexus` are used interchangeably.
5. **Test suite depends on the environment.** `make test` includes `security_gates.sh`, which needs network and npm config. That is why "green" has to be described as "388/390 with known failures". One worktree test is also flaky under full-suite load.
6. **Tool-layer defects.**
   - `search_code` returns misleading results for regex literals and broad concept searches.
   - `StreamRedactor` rewrites tool-call IDs to low-entropy hashes.
   - Your Phase 4 notes list many more, including redaction gaps (AWS secrets, URL credentials), diff-review blind spots (CRLF-only changes), and memory/frame-time worst cases.

## Assumptions that are incorrect

- **"Comparable to Codex CLI / Claude Code."** The README's feature table says this, but the dogfooding results don't support it. The supervised result was `READY_WITH_FRICTION`, and context engineering was `MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED`. The comparison is aspirational.
- **"The model stopping or a test passing means the task is done."** The repo already rejects this in `turn.ts`. The agent loop still behaves as if a green verifier is available when the baseline is red.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md` is stale.** It describes an IPC/CLI-subprocess split with the TypeScript layer on top. The default product is now a Ratatui TUI with a TypeScript sidecar speaking NDJSON. It also hard-codes "Dual Intel Arc A770 XPUs", which is a hardware assumption presented as architecture.
- **The dangerous-command filter is a security boundary.** `is_dangerous_command` is a pattern denylist (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, fork bombs). A denylist can't contain a shell, so the real boundaries have to be the authority layer, the path jail and the sandbox. The docs list it alongside them as an equal.
- **Secret redaction is complete.** Regex redaction misses known cases, and the stream redactor has damaged data (tool-call IDs).
- **More ceremony means more correctness.** The requirement matrices and closure assessments prove traceability, not that the agent is good at engineering. The evidence that matters is the dogfood and experiment results, and those say the agent loop is the weak point.
- **The inference substrate is the limiter.** Your last campaign was asking exactly this question. The evidence leans toward Nexus itself (evidence-to-decision failure, verification looping) rather than the local model.

## Suggested next slice

Fix baseline-aware verification (Part C) first. It's concrete, it has a reproduced failure, and it directly produces wasted agent steps. Then decide whether to merge the C2 compaction candidate. After that, commit or split off the 38 dirty Cloudflare files, untrack `cli/dist`, and rewrite `ARCHITECTURE.md` to match the TUI sidecar design.

I can start on Part C, or run `graphify` queries on any of these areas if you want more evidence first.
